digest.component_or_area: complexity baseline wrapper and ruff C901 lint gate
propositions: Raw Ruff exits 1 with 53 C901 diagnostics above threshold 15 in production code; the wrapper must accept this known debt without blocking changes while rejecting new or increased complexity.

A baseline JSON document with 53 ceiling entries maps qualified symbol keys (path::ast.ancestry) to integer scores; the wrapper compares current Ruff output against ceilings to compute active/new/increased/stale counters, failing only on new or increased debt.

The --update-stale maintenance mode lowers ceilings and removes stale entries through atomic_write, refusing to write if new/increased debt or scanner/schema errors exist, leaving the target file unchanged on all failure paths.

Ruff return codes 0 and 1 both proceed to JSON validation and counter comparison; return code 2 or greater, missing executable, invalid JSON, non-C901 output, or duplicate current keys makes the wrapper exit nonzero as a scanner failure.

Symbol identity derives from Python AST ancestry (nested functions, async methods, class hierarchy) normalized to repository-relative POSIX paths; lambdas and duplicate same-qualified-key diagnostics produce normalization failures rather than ambiguity.
